t: Introduction and overview — Mistral-class Amphibious Assault Ship
name: Introduction and overview — Mistral-class Amphibious Assault Ship — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Mistral-class Amphibious Assault Ship
description: Introduction and overview of the Mistral-class Amphibious Assault Ship: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. France's Mistral class — three French ships plus two sold to Egypt — are 21,300-ton helicopter carriers (BPC) with well decks, hospitals, and command facilities. They led French operations in Libya, Mali, and humanitarian missions. The two originally built for Russia were diverted to Egypt after 2014 sanctions. Baseline facts: French amphibious assault ship; 5 built (3 France, 2 Egypt); 21,300 tons..
how_it_works: Buoyancy supports the hull; propellers driven by diesel, turbine, or nuclear plant provide thrust; rudders and thrusters steer; stability comes from hull form and ballast.
key_points: Mistral-class Amphibious Assault Ship: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history.
French amphibious assault ship; 5 built (3 France, 2 Egypt); 21,300 tons.
Key figure: Two ex-Russia ships to Egypt; hospital + command; Libya/Mali operations.
